_sources.discrepancies: South Dakota requests photo ID — NCSL categorizes SD as 'photo ID requested'. Voters without photo ID may provide last four digits of SSN, sign a poll book affidavit, or be vouched for by an election judge. Primary is set by statute as the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June. 2026-06-10 verification: the 35% runoff provision was TRIGGERED for the first time in state history — no Republican candidate for Governor reached 35% in the June 2, 2026 primary, so a Republican gubernatorial runoff (secondary election) is scheduled for JULY 28, 2026 (file previously carried an Aug 4 estimate). Registration deadline for the runoff is July 13, 2026 (5 p.m.); absentee voting for the runoff began June 12, 2026 per the SD SoS. Note: because SD primaries are closed, the Republican runoff is open to voters eligible for the Republican primary — the earlier description of SD runoffs as open to any voter regardless of party was corrected. Primary absentee start corrected to the statutory 46th day (April 17, 2026; file previously had May 4). primaryParticipation.type aligned to 'closed' to match elections[].primaryType and the closed-primary reality (it was 'open', contradicting the rest of the file).

acceptedIds: South Dakota driver's license or state ID card
Photo ID issued by a South Dakota accredited university or college
votingRules.expirationRule: Photo ID should not be expired. If a voter lacks photo ID, they may sign a personal identification affidavit and vote a regular ballot.
votingRules.impedimentDeclaration: Voters without acceptable photo ID may provide the last four digits of their SSN plus sign a poll book affidavit, or be vouched for by an election judge who knows the voter.
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: South Dakota does not have a statewide prohibition on phones at polling places, but voters may not photograph their ballot or interfere with other voters. Check with your county auditor for local rules.
additionalRules: Closed primary: only voters registered with a party may vote in that party's primary.

Runoff (secondary election) rule: if no candidate for Governor, U.S. Senate, or U.S. House receives 35% of the primary vote, the top two advance to a runoff. The 2026 Republican gubernatorial runoff is July 28, 2026; closed-primary eligibility rules apply.
No runoffs in South Dakota general elections — the candidate with the most votes wins.

eligibility: Any registered voter may request an absentee ballot without providing a reason
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: Day before the election (received by county auditor) for mail ballot; in-person absentee voting available through the Monday before the election
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the county auditor by the time polls close on Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Must arrive at the county auditor by poll closing on Election Day. Postmarks do not count.

runoffRules.ruleExplanation: South Dakota rule: if no candidate for Governor, U.S. Senate, or U.S. House receives 35% of the primary vote, the top two advance to a runoff (secondary election). You are not locked to the runoff by having voted in the primary, but South Dakota primaries are closed, so a party's runoff is open only to voters eligible to vote in that party's primary. The 2026 Republican gubernatorial runoff is July 28, 2026.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: South Dakota primaries are closed: only voters registered with a party (or independents, where the party allows it) may vote that party's primary ballot. If no candidate for Governor, U.S. Senate, or U.S. House receives 35% of the vote, the top two advance to a runoff (secondary election); the same party eligibility rules apply to the runoff.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Las primarias de Dakota del Sur son cerradas: solo los votantes registrados con un partido (o independientes, cuando el partido lo permite) pueden votar la boleta primaria de ese partido. Si ningún candidato para Gobernador, Senado de EE. UU. o Cámara de EE. UU. obtiene el 35% de los votos, los dos primeros avanzan a una segunda vuelta (elección secundaria); las mismas reglas de elegibilidad de partido se aplican a la segunda vuelta.
